title: Design a Notification System
tagline: Deliver push, SMS, and email at scale — reliably, without duplicates, and without spamming users.
summary: Multi-channel delivery, queues, retries, dedup, rate/preferences.

blocks.title: Functional
items: Send notifications across channels: mobile push (APNs/FCM), SMS, email, in-app.
Triggered by events (someone liked your post) or campaigns (marketing blast).
Respect user preferences (opt-outs, channel choice) and quiet hours.

blocks.title: Non-functional
items: Reliable delivery with retries; no lost notifications.
Avoid duplicates (don't notify the same thing twice).
High throughput (millions/min for campaigns) with spike absorption.
Low latency for transactional notifications (OTP, alerts).

paragraphs: This is fundamentally an **asynchronous, queue-driven** system. A producer (any service) calls a Notification API; the system enriches, applies preferences/rate limits, then fans the request to per-channel queues, where channel workers call the external providers. Queues decouple bursty producers from rate-limited providers and provide retry/buffering.

blocks.caption: API → enrich + apply preferences → per-channel queues → workers → external providers.

items.title: Ingest
items.detail: A request hits the Notification API: {user_id, event_type, payload}. Validate and dedup (idempotency key per logical notification).

items.title: Resolve
items.detail: Look up the user's preferences, devices/contact info, and channel choices; drop opted-out channels; apply quiet hours and rate caps.

items.title: Template & enqueue
items.detail: Render the message per channel and enqueue to that channel's queue.

items.title: Deliver
items.detail: Channel workers pull from the queue and call the provider (APNs/FCM for push, Twilio for SMS, SES/SendGrid for email), respecting provider rate limits.

items.title: Track
items.detail: Record status (sent/delivered/failed/opened) via provider callbacks for analytics and retry decisions.
Queues deliver at-least-once, so workers may retry — make delivery idempotent with a dedup key (notification_id) so a user isn't notified twice for the same event.
Provider failures are common (transient). Retry with exponential backoff + jitter; cap attempts.
After max retries, move to a DLQ for inspection rather than retrying forever or dropping silently.
Have a secondary provider for critical channels (e.g., two SMS vendors) so one provider's outage doesn't stop OTPs.

blocks.title: The duplicate-notification trap
blocks.text: Without dedup, a retried or re-emitted event sends two 'You have a new message' pushes — a common, annoying bug. Key every logical notification with an idempotency id and check before sending.

items.detail: A campaign to 50M users floods the system; the queues buffer it and workers drain at the providers' allowed rate. Scale workers horizontally per channel.
Cap notifications per user per time window so a noisy event source can't spam someone — protects user experience and your sender reputation.
Separate transactional (OTP, security — low latency, high priority) from marketing (bulk, best-effort) using separate queues/priorities so a campaign never delays an OTP.
A preference service decides eligibility before enqueueing; respecting opt-outs/quiet hours is both UX and legal (CAN-SPAM/GDPR).

blocks.text: Key talking points: 'Async, queue-driven, per-channel workers; at-least-once + idempotent dedup; retries with backoff + DLQ; separate priority lanes for transactional vs marketing; preference/rate checks before send.' Mentioning provider rate limits and the duplicate trap shows production awareness.

cheatsheet: Notifications = async, queue-driven, multi-channel (push/SMS/email/in-app) with per-channel workers calling providers.
Flow: API → dedup + resolve preferences/devices → template → per-channel queue → worker → provider → track status.
At-least-once delivery → make sending idempotent with a notification-id dedup key (avoid double notifications).
Retries with exponential backoff + jitter; dead-letter queue after max attempts; secondary providers for critical channels.
Queues absorb campaign spikes; separate priority lanes so OTP/transactional never wait behind marketing.
Check user preferences/opt-outs/quiet hours + per-user rate caps before sending (UX + legal).

questions.prompt: A marketing campaign to 50M users is queued at the same time OTP login codes need to go out instantly. How do you ensure OTPs aren't delayed?
questions.hint: Don't let bulk traffic share a lane with time-critical traffic.
answer: Separate the traffic into **priority lanes / distinct queues**: a high-priority transactional queue (OTPs, security alerts) and a low-priority bulk queue (marketing). Workers service the transactional queue first (or it has dedicated, reserved worker capacity and provider quota), so a 50M-message campaign sitting in the bulk queue can't head-of-line-block an OTP. The campaign drains in the background at the providers' allowed rate.

Reinforce with: dedicated provider throughput/short codes for OTP, rate-limit/spread the campaign so it doesn't exhaust shared provider quota, and autoscale workers. The core principle is isolating latency-critical traffic from bulk best-effort traffic — a bulkhead applied to notifications.
keyPoints: Separate priority queues: transactional vs marketing
Dedicated/reserved capacity + provider quota for OTP
Campaign drains in background; can't block OTP (no head-of-line blocking)
followUps: How would you smooth a 50M campaign so it doesn't exhaust the email provider's rate limit?

questions.prompt: Why might a user receive the same push notification twice, and how do you prevent it?
answer: Queues deliver at-least-once and workers retry on transient failures, so the same notification can be processed more than once — e.g., a worker sends the push successfully but crashes before acking the message, so it's redelivered and sent again. The triggering event itself might also be emitted twice upstream.

Prevent it by making send **idempotent**: assign each logical notification a unique idempotency id (derived from the event, e.g., `notif:{user}:{event_id}`), and before sending, check a dedup store for that id; if already sent, skip. Record the id atomically with the send. This way retries and duplicate events result in exactly one notification reaching the user.
keyPoints: At-least-once + retries (and duplicate events) cause double sends
Check dedup store before sending; record atomically
Duplicates become no-ops → exactly one notification
followUps: What would you use as the idempotency key for a 'new message' push?
